newsitem.title: USA: BPA attributes peak power sales to lighter loads.
newsitem.headline: BPA attributes peak power sales to lighter loads.

text.p: Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) was able to resume next-day sales of surplus power during peak demand hours because warmer weather has cut regional demand, BPA trade sources said Tuesday.

After withholding peak sales for nearly a week, BPA for Wednesday offered up to 200 megawatts (MW) during peak hours at $14.00 for Northwest deliveries and $15.00 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales.
Another 500 MW of non-firm power was offered during morning and evening peaks at $15.00-16.00. Non-firm power for shoulder hours was offered at $12.00-13.00, with no volume limit.
"Our loads are lighter so we have more power to sell," said a BPA trader in Portland, Ore.
"Tomorrow loads will be even lighter," based on forecasts calling for further warming, he added.
BPA said generation at the Grand Coulee dam in Washington state is still being curtailed due to voltage support problems associated with the outage of a major transmission line.
The 500 kilovolt Raver-Schultz line, which runs from Snohomish County, Wash., to the Canadian border, was damaged in a Jan 17 ice storm.
A BPA spokeswoman said Monday repairs to the line would likely be completed by Wednesday.
